title: Russell 'Big Chief' Moore, Louis Armstrong and Jack Teagarden
summary: Fields names Chief as the best all-round player; Armstrong told him nobody plays like Chief, but Teagarden had the name.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now, what was the very last year that you were involved in your band as a bandleader, the very final year?

While we were talking about those soloists, it looked like the two I named were a little more flexible and could cover things, but just for outright blowing and sensational dixieland, "Big Chief" Russell Moore; I think he's the greatest all over.
And as I said, one time Louie Armstrong used to call me Oklahoma and Chief was with Louie after he left me, and I ran

across Louie shortly after that once, and that was when big bands were favored and he had his all star band, and he had Jack Teagarden on trombone; so I said Louie, that's something else, you took my man away from me and now it's you and Jack Teagarden. There's no way in the world he can play the horn like Chief. So he goes, you're right Oklahoma, but they wanted a name and that's all we got to name, but nobody plays a horn like Chief plays.
He needed a name so he got Teagarden?
I agree with you, Teagarden is all right, but far from what I would consider great, but again Glaser wanted somebody who was a drawing card and he got Teagarden.
I'm not that familiar with Chief's playing, but I would say that from what I did hear of him, I would like him better, because of his dixieland.
